long_biography.plain_text:
Van de Vyvere began as an office employee at a freight-forwarding company in the Port of Ghent. In 1985 he acquired a small coal terminal from a South African group, renamed it Ghent Coal Terminal and used that foothold to assemble SEA-invest. He expanded first across dry bulk and fruit handling, then into general cargo and containers.

A 2004 chemical-terminal acquisition opened liquid-bulk storage, which Van de Vyvere enlarged through major tank investments and partnerships. SEA-invest now operates terminals in more than twenty ports across Europe and Africa, combining cargo handling with storage, transport, customs and related logistics. Van de Vyvere remains the group's controller while preparing a durable family-succession structure.

uncertainties.detail: The SEA-invest owner is distinguished from Philippe Vande Vyvere associated with the Matexi family and from a Ghent Philippe Van de Vyvere born in 1957 who died in 2025. The source record's age, Belgian residence and spaced surname align with the SEA-invest founder born in August 1953, and the corporate, Forbes and regulated-prospectus chain makes that resolution very high confidence.

Forbes spells the profile heading 'Phillippe' with two consecutive p characters, but its body uses Philippe and the SEA-invest ownership, age, residence, citizenship and wealth source all identify this exact subject. The canonical source-record spelling is retained.

De Standaard gives 5 August 1953, French corporate records give August 1953, Forbes reports age 73 in September 2026, and the source record gives age 66 in May 2020. An indexed Belgian corporate-document transcription contains an inconsistent national-register prefix, likely an OCR defect; the convergence of the other sources supports 1953. Ghent birthplace rests on that exact-name corporate instrument and is proposed at slightly lower confidence.

French and Ivorian official records use the full legal name Philippe François Pierre Van de Vyvere. The immutable source has already placed 'van de' in the middle-names field and 'Vyvere' in the last-name field, so the dossier does not attempt to replace or expand that nonblank name data.

Forbes and De Standaard support a self-made origin through employment, acquisition and group building. One report notes a maternal connection to a port-industry family, while public sources do not disclose the financing of the initial acquisition or current equity percentages. The broad Self-made classification avoids overclaiming an independent start, and the biography says control rather than a precise percentage.

Focused searches found no verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website for the SEA-invest founder. A visible LinkedIn profile for a Philippe Van de Vyvere at Cosmos SA and two directory results belong to other people and are excluded; the company website is used as a source rather than proposed as a personal social.

Both biographies omit private-vessel facts, residential and lifestyle details, point-in-time net worth, private-company valuations, current transaction values and unrelated investments. Nothing has been compiled or applied.
